name: Honeywell Home T9 (US)

radios.note: Honeywell lists Wi-Fi (2.4 and 5 GHz). The room sensors link directly to the thermostat; the pages we saw don't name their radio.

matter.note: No Honeywell or CSA page found mentions Matter for the T9. Absence is not a statement that it lacks it.

apple_home.note: Honeywell's T9 user guide has a HomeKit pairing procedure (Connect HomeKit on the thermostat, then scan the code in the Home app). Its support article says HomeKit can change setpoints but cannot read the room sensors.

google_home.note: Honeywell says Google Assistant can view and control both the thermostat and its sensors.

alexa.note: Honeywell says Alexa can view and control both the thermostat and its sensors.

smartthings.note: Honeywell lists SmartThings. Its support article says SmartThings can change setpoints but cannot read the sensors.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's Honeywell integration is for Total Connect Comfort and lists other models; the docs seen do not name the T9. A forum user runs a T9 through HomeKit, which is not a maker source.

hubRequired.note: Built-in Wi-Fi; room sensors pair directly with the thermostat.

localControl.note: No maker source states what works without internet.

systems.value: Most 24 V heat, cool and heat pump systems
systems.note: Honeywell's guide says it does not work with electric baseboard (120-240 V) or millivolt systems. Contact a pro for line voltage, dual fuel or fan coil setups. One record covers the RCHT9510WFW (no sensor) and RCHT9610WFSW (with sensor), which share the same installation guide.

power.note: Honeywell says the T9 needs 24 V through a C-wire and ships with a C-wire adapter for homes without one. The install guide says adapter installation is more complicated on zoned systems.

summary: Honeywell Home sells the T9 as a US Wi-Fi wall thermostat with optional wireless room sensors, and it needs 24 V on a C-wire (an adapter is included). Alexa and Google Assistant can read the thermostat and sensors, while HomeKit and SmartThings can only change setpoints, according to Honeywell. It suits most 24 V heat, cool and heat pump systems. Home Assistant and Matter support are not confirmed.
caveats: HomeKit and SmartThings cannot read room sensor values, per Honeywell's support article.
A C-wire is required; the supplied adapter covers homes without one, but Honeywell says fitting it on zoned systems is more complicated and suggests a pro.
Not for electric baseboard or millivolt systems.
